theorems.name: vvunop__is_wf
theorems.proof:

  rintro ⟨_, -⟩ - hv rfl
  exact inot__is_wf _ _ _ hv rfl
theorems.notes: fun_vvunop_ has one constructor (V128, NOT). After rintro, v_vectype is V128 and the result is inot_ (Option.get! (size valtype.V128)) v128, which is definitionally the conclusion's width. No reasoning about Option.get! none or default. The `size ≠ none` premise is not needed. Axioms: inot__is_wf, propext.

theorems.name: vvbinop__is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro (⟨_, _, -⟩ | ⟨_, _, -⟩ | ⟨_, _, -⟩ | ⟨_, _, -⟩) - h1 h2 rfl
  · exact iand__is_wf _ _ _ _ h1 h2 rfl
  · exact iandnot__is_wf _ _ _ _ h1 h2 rfl
  · exact ior__is_wf _ _ _ _ h1 h2 rfl
  · exact ixor__is_wf _ _ _ _ h1 h2 rfl
theorems.notes: Four constructors (AND/ANDNOT/OR/XOR), each closed by the generated axiom for its operation. The rintro patterns must name every explicit field (`⟨_, _, -⟩`): a short pattern like `⟨-⟩` silently mis-binds the later intro names. Axioms: iand__is_wf, iandnot__is_wf, ior__is_wf, ixor__is_wf, propext.

theorems.name: vunop__is_wf
theorems.notes:

In those four cases, `var_0_lst` is tied to the lanes only by the zip-based `Forall₂ (fun y l => fun_iabs_ ...) var_0_lst lane_1_lst`, and there is no `List.length var_0_lst = List.length lane_1_lst` premise (the old model had one). So `var_0_lst` can carry extra, ill-formed elements, and the result `inv_lanes_ sh (Map mk var_0_lst)` is outside what `inv_lanes__is_wf` covers. If you want the sorry confined to those 4 cases, here is a partial replacement for `:=\n  sorry`. It compiles in /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-spectec/14eafe93-c912-45da-8e28-e9b09c1a6ef6/scratchpad/agents/g3-vector-a/Partial.lean and needs the helpers iswf_inv_lanes_map and iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map, which need iswf_Forall_setproduct*:
:= by

  subst heq
  cases h <;> subst_vars
  all_goals first
    | exact absurd rfl hne

How it works: case_26 (result `none`) is refuted by `var_0 ≠ none`. Cases 4-11 (NEG/POPCNT) use the premise `Forall (fun l => wf_lane_ (fun_lanetype sh) (op l)) lane_1_lst`. Cases 12-25 (float ops via setproduct_) use the nested Forall premise. Nothing depends on default values.

helpers.name: iswf_Forall_Map₂
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_Forall_Map₂ {α β γ : Type} {P : γ → Prop} (f : α → β → γ) :
    ∀ (l1 : List α) (l2 : List β), Forall₂ (fun a b => P (f a b)) l1 l2 → Forall P (Map₂ f l1 l2)
  | [], _, _ => fun _ hx => by simp [Map₂, List.ap] at hx
  | _ :: _, [], _ => fun _ hx => by simp [Map₂, List.ap] at hx
  | a :: l1, b :: l2, h => fun x hx => by
    simp only [Map₂, List.ap, List.map_cons, List.zipWith_cons_cons, List.mem_cons] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · exact h (a, b) (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    · exact iswf_Forall_Map₂ f l1 l2 (fun t ht => h t (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ht)) x hx
helpers.notes: Same name and statement as the old helper and as g4-vector-b's port (only the proof differs), so the merge can keep a single copy. None of my proved theorems uses it; it is used by iswf_inv_lanes_map₂, iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map₂ and the partial vbinop proof.

helpers.name: iswf_Forall_setproduct2
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_Forall_setproduct2 {X : Type} {P : X → Prop} (w : X) (hw : P w) :
    ∀ (lls : List (List X)), Forall (Forall P) lls → Forall (Forall P) (setproduct2_ X w lls)
  | [], _ => iswf_Forall_nil _
  | l :: lls, h =>
    iswf_Forall_append
      (iswf_Forall_cons (iswf_Forall_append (iswf_Forall_cons hw (iswf_Forall_nil _)) (h l (List.mem_cons_self ..)))
        (iswf_Forall_nil _))
      (iswf_Forall_setproduct2 w hw lls (fun m hm => h m (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hm)))
helpers.notes: Structural recursion. It replaces the old iswf_setproduct2 under a new name because the statement uses `Forall (Forall P)` and a different argument order. Needed only by iswf_Forall_setproduct1.

helpers.name: iswf_Forall_setproduct1
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_Forall_setproduct1 {X : Type} {P : X → Prop} (lls : List (List X)) (hlls : Forall (Forall P) lls) :
    ∀ (l : List X), Forall P l → Forall (Forall P) (setproduct1_ X l lls)
  | [], _ => iswf_Forall_nil _
  | w :: l, h =>
    iswf_Forall_append (iswf_Forall_setproduct2 w (h w (List.mem_cons_self ..)) lls hlls)
      (iswf_Forall_setproduct1 lls hlls l (fun x hx => h x (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx)))
helpers.notes: Placed after iswf_Forall_setproduct2. Needed only by iswf_Forall_setproduct.

helpers.name: iswf_Forall_setproduct
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_Forall_setproduct {X : Type} {P : X → Prop} :
    ∀ (lls : List (List X)), Forall (Forall P) lls → Forall (Forall P) (setproduct_ X lls)
  | [], _ => iswf_Forall_cons (iswf_Forall_nil _) (iswf_Forall_nil _)
  | l :: lls, h =>
    iswf_Forall_setproduct1 _ (iswf_Forall_setproduct lls (fun m hm => h m (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hm))) l
      (h l (List.mem_cons_self ..))
helpers.notes: setproduct_ keeps elementwise properties. Generic, so it can be reused by any vector theorem whose float results go through setproduct_. Used by the two setproduct inv_lanes helpers.

helpers.name: iswf_inv_lanes_map
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_inv_lanes_map {α : Type} {sh : shape} {f : α → lane_} {l : List α} (hsh : wf_shape sh)
    (h : Forall (fun x => wf_lane_ (fun_lanetype sh) (f x)) l) :
    Forall (fun v => wf_uN 128 v) [inv_lanes_ sh (Map f l)] :=
  iswf_Forall_cons (inv_lanes__is_wf _ _ _ hsh (iswf_Forall_map _ _ h (fun _ hx => hx)) rfl) (iswf_Forall_nil _)
helpers.notes: Shaped to match the `some [inv_lanes_ sh (Map f lanes)]` results of the vector relations, so that `exact iswf_inv_lanes_map ‹_› ‹_›` closes a case after `subst_vars`. Used by the partial vunop proof (cases 4-11).

helpers.name: iswf_inv_lanes_map₂
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_inv_lanes_map₂ {α β : Type} {sh : shape} {f : α → β → lane_} {l1 : List α} {l2 : List β}
    (hsh : wf_shape sh) (h : Forall₂ (fun a b => wf_lane_ (fun_lanetype sh) (f a b)) l1 l2) :
    Forall (fun v => wf_uN 128 v) [inv_lanes_ sh (Map₂ f l1 l2)] :=
  iswf_Forall_cons (inv_lanes__is_wf _ _ _ hsh (iswf_Forall_Map₂ _ _ _ h) rfl) (iswf_Forall_nil _)
helpers.notes: Used by the partial vbinop proof (cases 0-7, 24-35). g4 has a similar iswf_inv_lanes_of_Forall₂_Map₂ that concludes wf_uN 128 (inv_lanes_ …) rather than the singleton Forall. The names differ, so there is no clash.

helpers.name: iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map {α β : Type} {sh : shape} {g : β → lane_} {k : α → List β} {l : List α}
    (hsh : wf_shape sh) (h : Forall (fun x => Forall (fun y => wf_lane_ (fun_lanetype sh) (g y)) (k x)) l) :
    Forall (fun v => wf_uN 128 v) (Map (fun ls => inv_lanes_ sh ls) (setproduct_ lane_ (Map (fun x => Map g (k x)) l))) :=
  iswf_Forall_map _ _ (iswf_Forall_setproduct _ (iswf_Forall_map _ _ h (fun _ hx => iswf_Forall_map _ _ hx (fun _ hy => hy))))
    (fun _ hls => inv_lanes__is_wf _ _ _ hsh hls rfl)
helpers.notes: Used by the partial vunop proof (float cases 12-25). The relations' premises say `wf_lane_ (lanetype_Fnn F)`, not `fun_lanetype sh`, but the two are definitionally equal, so `‹_›` finds the premise.

helpers.name: iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map₂
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_inv_lanes_setproduct_map₂ {α β γ : Type} {sh : shape} {g : γ → lane_} {k : α → β → List γ}
    {l1 : List α} {l2 : List β} (hsh : wf_shape sh)
    (h : Forall₂ (fun a b => Forall (fun y => wf_lane_ (fun_lanetype sh) (g y)) (k a b)) l1 l2) :
    Forall (fun v => wf_uN 128 v)
      (Map (fun ls => inv_lanes_ sh ls) (setproduct_ lane_ (Map₂ (fun a b => Map g (k a b)) l1 l2))) :=
  iswf_Forall_map _ _
    (iswf_Forall_setproduct _ (iswf_Forall_Map₂ _ _ _ (fun t ht => iswf_Forall_map _ _ (h t ht) (fun _ hy => hy))))
    (fun _ hls => inv_lanes__is_wf _ _ _ hsh hls rfl)
helpers.notes: Used by the partial vbinop proof (float cases 36-51). All 8 helpers are in Final.lean and compile with no sorry, but none of the 3 proved theorems uses them: they matter only if the partial vunop/vbinop proofs are merged, or if other vector proofs reuse them. Otherwise they can be dropped.

issues: vunop__is_wf and vbinop__is_wf cannot be proved as generated (they are independent of the model, not refutable). The regenerated fun_vunop_ cases 0-3 (ABS on integer lanes) and fun_vbinop_ cases 8-23 (MIN/MAX/ADD_SAT/SUB_SAT) bind the result list `var_0_lst` only through Forall₂/Forall₃. These are defined with `List.zip`, so they say nothing about elements past the lane list's length. The old model had `List.length var_0_lst = List.length lane_1_lst` (and the same for var_1_lst); the new one has neither. So `var_0_lst` may contain arbitrary ill-formed values, and the result `inv_lanes_ sh (Map mk var_0_lst)` involves the opaque inv_lanes_, whose only axiom (inv_lanes__is_wf) requires every lane to be well formed. The statements are true only under the opaque's implementation value (Inhabited.default), which proofs cannot use and the brief forbids.

Machine-checked witness, no sorry, axioms lanes__is_wf/propext/Quot.sound: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-spectec/14eafe93-c912-45da-8e28-e9b09c1a6ef6/scratchpad/agents/g3-vector-a/Witness.lean. `gap_vbinop_min_u_instance junk` and `gap_vunop_abs_instance junk` build valid fun_vbinop_ (i32x4.min_u) and fun_vunop_ (i32x4.abs) instances on the zero vector, with any `junk : uN` appended to var_0_lst. `gap_vbinop__is_wf_consequence` and `gap_vunop__is_wf_consequence` take the generated statements as hypotheses and derive `wf_uN 128 (inv_lanes_ i32x4 (… ++ [mk_lane__0 I32 junk]))`. `gap_junk_lane_not_wf` shows junk = 2^32 gives an ill-formed lane. WitnessCheck.lean in the same folder type-checks these against the real imported theorems, so the hypotheses are exactly the generated statements.

Likely backend cause: with Sideconditions now running before DefToRel, no length side condition is emitted for the fresh list that DefToRel introduces when it turns an iterated function call (`$iabs_(N, lane)*`, `$imin_(...)*`, ...) into an iterated relation premise `Forall₂/₃ (fun_R … var_k_elem) var_k_lst lanes`. Suggested fixes: emit `|var_k_lst| = |lanes|` there, as the old pipeline did, or make Forall₂/Forall₃ require equal lengths. Separately, DefToRel emits each such call twice (var_2_lst for the wf premise, var_0_lst for the result); this redundancy is why the old proofs needed determinism lemmas.

Partial proofs that prove every other case and keep `sorry` only in those 20 cases (4 in vunop, 16 in vbinop) are in /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-spectec/14eafe93-c912-45da-8e28-e9b09c1a6ef6/scratchpad/agents/g3-vector-a/Partial.lean; the texts are in the theorem notes. Once the length premise is restored, the remaining cases follow from lanes__is_wf plus the existing iabs__is_wf / imin__is_wf / imax__is_wf / iadd_sat__is_wf / isub_sat__is_wf. This works directly on var_0_lst and does not need the duplicate var_2_lst.

Heads-up for other agents: a scan of the regenerated file finds the same 'relation-produced list with no length premise' pattern in fun_vcvtop__ cases 0-2 and in Step_pure.vshiftop. In both, the unconstrained list feeds inv_lanes_ and the produced lanes have no wf premise, so vcvtop___is_wf and the vshiftop case of Step_pure_is_wf probably hit the same wall. fun_vrelop_ cases 8-23 and Step_pure.vbitmask also have the pattern but carry a wf premise on the actual output, so they are unaffected. fun_utf8_case_4 and fun_allocmodule_case_0 also match the scan; I did not inspect them.
